correctness.rationale: Represent the order statistics M,A=(S∓|D|)/2, S=X+Y, D=X−Y. The symmetric Skellam pmf, telescoping k I_k(z)=z(I_{k-1}−I_{k+1})/2 and I0/I1 derivatives give d=E|D|=2λq, d'(λ)=2r. Differentiate the joint Poisson series: Cov(S,|D|)=λ d'=2λr. Since Var(S)=Var(D)=2λ and Var(|D|)=2λ−d², bilinear expansion gives claimed variances. Standard fixed-order Bessel expansion yields q=(πλ)^(-1/2)(1−1/(16λ)+O(λ^-2)), r=(2√(πλ))^-1(1+1/(16λ)+O(λ^-2)); expansion proves both Fano corrections. Independently double summed all joint Poisson cells 0..89 at λ=0.5,3,9 to 35-digit accuracy for four moments. Exact proof not finite extrapolation.

value.rationale: This is a motivated sharp quantitative answer to the Poisson order-statistic underdispersion question: exact finite-intensity noise for both extremes and a nontrivial universal asymptotic deficit 1/π and first-order direction. It is more than a rewording of the generic ultra-log-concavity theorem; n=2 is the first nontrivial paired-extreme case.
residual_risks: Scope restricted to two independent equal-intensity Poisson counts.

final_claim: For two iid Poisson(λ) counts, λ>0, let q=e^{-2λ}(I0(2λ)+I1(2λ)), r=e^{-2λ}I0(2λ). The min/max means are λ(1∓q), variances λ(1∓r−λq²), and both Fano factors tend to 1−1/π with respective ±((1/2−1/π)/√π)λ^{-1/2} corrections.
